title: Canonical boundary adjunction, evaluation and projection-transpose data
statement: Work with the size convention [def-weil-size-convention] and the ordinary unbounded constant-coefficient module derived categories $D(W_{et},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For a finite commutative ring $A$ and a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], define the canonical boundary adjunction data as follows. Put $s=Li^*$ (the exact constant-coefficient inverse image), $F=Ri_*=Ri_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and let $G$ be the selected right adjoint of $F$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] [lem-exc-closed-ambient], with counit $\mu:FG\to id$. Tensor and internal Hom are the ordinary derived tensor and $R\mathcal Hom_A$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and $\sigma$ is the canonical signed tensor symmetry [lem-kun-tensor-sym] [lem-amb-derived-tensor-symmetry-involutive]. The projection $\pi_{B,M}:FB\otimes^L M\to F(B\otimes^L sM)$ is the canonical projection transformation [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. For each specified invertible component $\pi_{GN,M}$, define $q_{M,N}:sM\otimes^L GN\to G(M\otimes^L N)$ as the $F\dashv G$ transpose of $F(\sigma_{sM,GN})$, followed by $\pi_{GN,M}^{-1}$, then $\sigma_{FGN,M}$, then $1_M\otimes\mu_N$. For any $W\in D(T_{et},A)$ put $D_TK=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,W)$ and $D_ZB=R\mathcal Hom_A(B,GW)$; evaluation $ev_K:D_TK\otimes^L K\to W$ is the tensor-Hom counit after the signed swap. Define $r_K=\sigma_{GD_TK,sK}$ followed by $q_{K,D_TK}$ followed by $G(\sigma_{K,D_TK}\,;ev_K)$, and $\alpha_K:GD_TK\to D_ZsK$ as the tensor-Hom transpose of $r_K$. The associated boundary Hom chain is the independent composite of exceptional adjunction, tensor-Hom, symmetry, inverse projection, exceptional adjunction, and tensor-Hom with symmetry; its source and target are $Hom(B,GD_TK)$ and $Hom(B,D_ZsK)$. None of these definitions asserts invertibility of $\alpha$ or biduality. The same formulas are packaged for abstract categories and bifunctors equipped with these adjunctions, natural projection components and involutive symmetries; canonical specialization supplies all of that data rather than accepting arbitrary maps. For the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a coefficient prime $\ell$ and finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], the finite coefficient ring is the canonical universe lift of $\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1}$, $n\in\mathbf N$. For a separated finite-type structure map $a_T:T\to Spec(k)$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-proper-morphism], define $\omega_T=a_T^\times A$, $\omega_Z=G\omega_T$, and the corresponding functors $D_T,D_Z$ by the preceding formulas.
